title: One copy hands off both the redlined picture and its spec list
goal: Handing a redline to a teammate takes two copies today: Copy Image for the picture, then Copy as Spec List for the text. When a document has measurements, Copy Image should put the spec list on the clipboard as text beside the picture, so pasting into a document or chat drops the picture and pasting into a plain text field drops the list, with nothing extra to learn.
notes: Open thread from the 2026-09-01 manager pass. Code: EditorState.copyCompositeToClipboard writes .png and .tiff only (Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift:546); copyMeasureSpecList already builds the text via MeasureSpecList.render(document:name:). NSPasteboard lets one item carry several types; declare the image types first so image-aware apps take them. Verify the paste order claim in real apps: some chat clients take the string when both exist, which is the thing to test before committing. Flag next-measure-panel; Current unchanged with the flag off.
acceptance: In the Next release with next-measure-panel on and at least one measurement: Copy Image (or the inspector Export section button), then paste into Notes or TextEdit, and the picture lands; paste into a plain text field (Spotlight, Terminal, a Safari address bar) and the spec list lands.

Pasting into Messages, Slack or Mail pastes the picture, not the text; this is checked by hand on at least two of them on the probe app before shipping. If any of them prefers the text, the change is withdrawn and a decision is opened with the observed behaviour instead.
A document with no measurements copies exactly what it copies today.

The Copied pill says what landed (picture, and the list when present); tests pin the pasteboard representations; Scripts/test.sh green; audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task.

log.note: Review before building: the idea holds. A first-time user does nothing new, the same Copy Image key hands off both. Risk is only in consumers that take the string when both exist; NSTextView's readable-type order (probed) puts TIFF and PNG before the string for rich text views and the string first for plain text views, which is exactly the split wanted. A header-only list (measurements exist but all hidden) is dropped: it says nothing the picture does not and would leave a stray line in a plain field. Shape: CompositeCopy in PhotonzCore pins the flavors and their order (png, tiff, then text); EditorState walks that list. Gated on next-measure-panel, Current untouched.

Built: CompositeCopy (PhotonzCore) + CompositeCopyTests pin flavors png, tiff, text and the header-only rule; EditorState.copyCompositeToClipboard walks the list behind next-measure-panel and raises the Copied pill (Image / Image and spec list with N measurements). Scripts/test.sh: 1235 tests green. Paste probe (swift script writing the same three flavors): rich NSTextView with graphics -> picture; WebKit contenteditable (Mail compose) -> picture; plain NSTextView, NSTextField, rich view without graphics -> list. Probe app builds and launches. NOT done: the by-hand Messages/Slack/Mail check. This agent has no Automation or Accessibility permission, so it cannot paste into other apps; the audit's step 5 hands that check to the user with the withdrawal rule spelled out in evaluate. Shipped behind the flag, which is off by default.

Copy Image (Shift-Cmd-C and the inspector Export button) now carries the spec list as text beside the PNG and TIFF when a visible measurement exists, behind next-measure-panel. CompositeCopy in PhotonzCore pins the flavors and order with tests; Scripts/test.sh green (1235). Paste probe: rich text views and a WebKit editable take the picture, plain fields take the list. Chat clients could not be driven unmanned; audit queue/audits/2026-09-02-copy-image-spec-list.json asks the user to try Messages and Slack and says when to withdraw.
